missionPremise: CTX-RETIRE closed 2026-09-09 having built recordRetirement into the LDT bake and handed this lane a six-rule walk-grading implementation under key walkGradingRuleProposal in its own close (_inbox/2026-09-09_ctx-retire_close.json), read in full per the dispatch's instruction rather than working from the dispatch's own summary. The integration seat rebuilt and pinned the publish image (_LDT_SHA=3885efad) so the bake writes recordRetirement, but never implemented the walk side, so Caldwell staging walk 716c7ad0 sits at pass=85 fail=1 on the survivor 48055:1 (HTTP 422). Source: _dispatches/2026-09-09_ctx-walkrule_dispatch.md.

planBeforeBuild.sixRules: Implement exactly the six rules verbatim from walkGradingRuleProposal: (1) read payload.recordRetirement, apply the REAL isEarnedRecordRetirement, never a bare truthy check; (2) an earned retirement grades its own class RETIRED, never BP-CONTENT-01, counted as retiredCount alongside servedCount; (3) BP-CONFORMANT-01 unchanged; (4) BP-CONTENT-01 unchanged at the leaf level; (5) any coverage/completeness metric excludes retired rows from its denominator; (6) prove the recognition check can REJECT a malformed marker before trusting it. Rules 3/4 are read as instructions NOT to widen either check -- plan is to insert the retirement branch strictly BETWEEN the existing BP-CONFORMANT-01 check and the existing BP-CONTENT-01 call in gradeParcelResponse (src/jobs/verify-walk.mjs), touching neither function's own internals.
planBeforeBuild.importNotReimplement: The dispatch is explicit: isEarnedRecordRetirement lives in LDT and must be IMPORTED, not reimplemented, unlike the existing REQUIRED_TIER1_FACET_PATHS mirror-plus-divergence-test pattern this file already uses for a static list. A predicate is riskier to hand-mirror than a list (DEV_PROCESS 2.4, the CTRL-1 shape: one rule, two implementations, free to disagree). Plan: add a new esbuild entry to the EXISTING scripts/build-publish-bake-clis.mjs (which already bundles four LDT CLI entrypoints into the Cloud publish image) that bundles lib/nodeFacetBakeTier1Conformant.ts itself, and a new src/lib/record-retirement.mjs that imports it at runtime -- from the Cloud image's BAKE_CLI_ROOT when set, or by bundling the LDT source on demand for local/dev/test. Risk flagged before building: this file's own import graph may pull in workspace packages or module-level side effects (a shared DB client, for instance) that behave differently at import time versus at the CLI entrypoints' own more complete bootstrapping -- to be verified against the real pinned SHA before trusting the mechanism, not assumed.
planBeforeBuild.the422: Diagnose before implementing, per the dispatch. Two candidate mechanisms: (A) the retirement is served and the walk simply has no rule for it (rule 2 fixes it) or (B) something else refuses the parcel entirely before any body is produced (rule 2 cannot fix it). Plan: read gradeParcelResponse's control flow first (does a non-ok HTTP response already short-circuit before any body-dependent check?), then verify live against the real staging endpoint rather than assume the dispatch's own historical guess (ACCESS_NOT_DEFAULTED) is still the cause.
planBeforeBuild.the48055Parcel: CTX-RETIRE found 48055:1 is likely a sentinel/bucket id (203 txgio_parcel features sharing prop_id='1'), not a real CAD account. Plan: answer the disposition question in the close (is it a real account, should it be graded at all) but do NOT touch the sampler (explicitly forbidden) and do NOT invent a new grading class outside the six rules to silently exclude it -- if evidence points to exclusion being correct, name it as an out-of-scope, operator-facing finding (DEV_PROCESS 5.4: propose, do not unilaterally remediate) rather than coding around it.
planBeforeBuild.verifyByViolating: Rule 6 requires proving the real predicate rejects a malformed marker. Plan: a test that loads the REAL isEarnedRecordRetirement from the pinned LDT source (skips with a named reason when the local environment lacks a pinned LDT checkout, matching the existing REQUIRED_TIER1_FACET_PATHS divergence test's own skip convention), pastes both a RUN 1 (a bare-truthy stand-in wrongly accepting the malformed marker) and RUN 2 (the real predicate correctly rejecting it) literally in the test body as assertions, not narrated.
